records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Midland oilman and cofounder/CEO of CrownQuest Operating, a Permian Basin oil-and-gas producer; a lay preacher who is one of Texas's most influential conservative financiers

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Occidental Petroleum agreed to buy CrownRock L.P. (the venture of Dunn's CrownQuest and Lime Rock Partners) in a deal valued at about $12 billion; Dunn and family were reported to hold roughly a 20% stake worth more than $2 billion

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Formed the political group Empower Texans in 2006, which he chaired and was its primary financial contributor, using it to back primary challengers against Republicans it deemed insufficiently conservative

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Bankrolled the Empower Texans network, including the dark-money arm Texans for Fiscal Responsibility (which scores legislators on a fiscal index) and the media arm Texas Scorecard
Gave at least $9.85 million to the Defend Texas Liberty PAC since the beginning of 2022, his main vehicle for exerting political influence

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Reported by Texas Monthly to have become 'the largest individual source of campaign money in the state by far'

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Serves as vice chairman of the Texas Public Policy Foundation and has served on the board of the First Liberty Institute

records.recipient: Texans United for a Conservative Majority
records.label: After the Nick Fuentes controversy, Dunn and Farris Wilks wound down Defend Texas Liberty and funded a new PAC, Texans United for a Conservative Majority, seeding it with about $2 million

records.contributor: Defend Texas Liberty PAC (principally funded by Tim Dunn and Farris Wilks)
records.label: The Dunn/Wilks-funded PAC gave $3 million to Dan Patrick in June 2023, as Patrick prepared to preside over AG Ken Paxton's impeachment trial in the Texas Senate

records.subject: Tim Dunn
records.label: Dunn's network spent heavily in the 2024 Republican primaries backing challengers to Texas House Republicans who had voted to impeach Ken Paxton

disputes.subject: Tim Dunn
disputes.label: Texas Monthly's 2024 profile characterized Dunn as a billionaire who 'wants to turn Texas into a Christian theocracy' and as financing efforts against public education and renewable energy; the characterization is the outlet's framing, not an adjudicated fact

disputes.subject: Tim Dunn
disputes.label: In October 2023, the then-president of the Dunn/Wilks-funded Defend Texas Liberty PAC (Jonathan Stickland) was reported to have hosted white nationalist Nick Fuentes for hours; Dunn later called the meeting 'a serious blunder' and the PAC was wound down

disputes.subject: Tim Dunn
disputes.label: Critics and some faith commentators have described Dunn as a Christian nationalist, a label he has rejected; the dispute concerns how to characterize his stated religious-political aims
